problem: The quiz asks 'Why does VR not need SLAM while AR does?' and the answer states VR never has to know the room. Six-degree-of-freedom VR headsets without base stations (standalone and inside-out tracked ones) compute their own head pose with visual-inertial SLAM. What VR does not need is a map of the room or registration of content to real surfaces. A student who writes 'VR never uses SLAM' in an exam will be marked wrong.
fix: Ask instead: 'Why does VR not need to register content to the real room, while AR does?' Answer: VR draws every pixel itself, so it needs only the user's pose in its own coordinate frame. That self-tracking is obtained by SLAM or visual-inertial odometry in modern headsets, but no real-world map and no world registration is required. AR draws on a view of the real room, so it must know where the camera is relative to real surfaces.

where: Section 1, 'The definition used in this chapter'
problem: The definition says MR anchors virtual objects to real surfaces and occludes them, but plain phone AR also anchors content to a detected plane (the table itself says AR knows 'a plane'). Anchoring alone therefore does not separate AR from MR, and a student may think it does.
fix: Say: MR = AR plus per-pixel depth of the real scene. Anchoring to a plane or marker already exists in AR; what MR adds is metric depth, so virtual content is placed in 3D and correctly hidden by real objects.

problem: The occlusion formula (hidden if z_v > z_r) is dropped in the middle of the content, interaction, mobility, cost and safety bullets, after Safety. It belongs with Test 3, where occlusion is explained. The section heading also omits mobility, which has its own bullet.
fix: Move the formula and the depth-buffer explanation into Section 1 under Test 3, and rename the heading 'Content, interaction, mobility, cost and safety'.

problem: The output gives bare numbers 0.3 and 0.15 without units, though the answer line carries metres.
fix: Write the output as 0.3 m and 0.15 m.

problem: 'it cannot run the test hidden if z_v > z_r' reads as broken English and can confuse a second-language reader.
fix: Write: 'Without z_r the app cannot check whether z_v > z_r, so it gives no answer and simply draws the virtual object on top.'

problem: 'A headset with the depth sensing that MR occlusion needs costs the most of the three' is stated as a general rule, but some high-end VR headsets cost more than depth-sensing AR/MR headsets.
fix: Qualify it: 'In the usual consumer range, phone AR is cheapest, a plain VR headset comes next, and a headset with real-scene depth for occlusion costs the most.'
